items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I said, “On this song on letter B, Conte you play a hundred choruses, on C Frank Rosolino, you have two thousand choruses,” we had to open it up.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well I was going to do this in the studio. This was done in the studio. But they want you in the studio, not rehearsing in a hall somewhere. So I had all this music. In the meantime there was a club that was going to close call The Seville. And the movie columnist called Eve Star took a liking to how I played and she knew the club owner at The Seville, and they were going to go out of business. They tried Latin, they tried all this, they had to try jazz. So they hired me with a quintet. They said five…

pieces of music and I said, “On this song on letter B, Conte you play a hundred choruses, on C Frank Rosolino, you have two thousand choruses,” we had to open it up. We’ll make backgrounds you know. And so we started to walk out to play, and there were 300 people packed in the club with a line waiting to get in. And you saw faces like Fred McMurray and Ginger Rodgers. All these movie stars. And all the musicians in town. So I called the band back in the dressing room. I said, “We’re starting a band tonight, but…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Frank Rossolino, I’ve got to tell you, with the Dream Band. Frank — everybody loved Frank Rossolino and the band.

ctx.x: Well I’ve really enjoyed this and I want to close with the last thing you wrote in your book, and it said, “Even though we know that into each life a little rain must fall, all in all I’ve been very fortunate for I’ve been able to laugh all the way to the bandstand.”

Yeah well it’s true. It really is true, Monk. I’ve been fortunate. ‘Cause I looked forward to getting on stage. I’m at my most comfortable when I’m on stage. Because I don’t work, I have fun. I mean I include my audience, that’s why I don’t like playing big concerts. If I play for people playing in a ballroom at least the audience is close, they’re about two feet away from me so I can tell the guy to get a toupee or whatever, I’m going to tell the guy. Lady get your nose fixed, or whatever it is. I become Don…
Well you figured out how to make it all work and I really admire it. And you’ve made some wonderful —
